I read the only test file and the `UnitData.update` implementation. The test suite parameterizes 24 cases, and every test does the same thing: create a fresh `UnitData()` and call `unit_data.update(data)` once.

From `category.py`, `update` first normalizes `data` to an object array, then iterates `for val in OrderedDict.fromkeys(data)`. That means the loop sees each unique element from `data` once, in insertion order. At the assignment site, the code is guarded by `if val not in self._mapping:` immediately before `self._mapping[val] = next(self._counter)`.

Because each test uses a brand-new `UnitData()`, the mapping starts empty for that test. Within a single `update` call, once a value has been seen, `OrderedDict.fromkeys(data)` prevents that same value from being iterated again. So every time line 221 executes, it is only after the condition `val not in self._mapping` evaluated true in line 220.
